title: The memory ledger of a 20-turn conversation: sliding window vs summary

events.label: Turn 1: constraints set
events.detail: "Budget under ¥500, dark colors only, invoice to the company name." — three hard constraints, the anchors of this task.

events.label: An ordinary reply
events.detail: The window is still roomy and all history sits verbatim in context — at this point 'memory' is just another name for the window.

events.label: Turn 12 approached
events.detail: Window 8192 (E04's ledger), history already at 5200 — near the ceiling, a memory decision is due.

events.label: Decision point: it no longer fits
events.detail: Two roads: sliding window — drop the oldest turns, simplest to build; summary — compress old history into a paragraph, aiming to keep fidelity.

events.label: Sliding window executes
events.detail: Only the last 6 turns are kept; turn 1's three constraints are dropped wholesale — no alarm rings when they fall out.

events.label: Turn 20: checkout
events.detail: "Place the order per my original requirements and issue the invoice." — 'original requirements' points at turn 1.

events.label: Sliding-window answer
events.detail: Turn 1 is not in the window: budget and invoice name are guessed — a personal-name invoice at ¥620. The model is not at fault; the context it was fed is.

events.label: Sliding-window ledger
events.detail: Memory ledger: history 4600 tokens, turn 1 constraints retained 0/3 — the window was saved and the task was lost.

events.label: Summary compresses
events.detail: The first 12 turns are folded into a roughly 200-token summary with all three constraints written into its body — a summary is compression, not disposal.

events.label: Summary ledger
events.detail: Memory ledger: history 5200 → 1800 (summary 200 + last 8 turns 1600), constraints retained 3/3. Window usage down 65%, information kept.

events.label: Summary answer
events.detail: Constraints read back from the summary: total ¥478, dark colors, company invoice — correct. The same model; only the memory strategy differs.

events.label: Both versions delivered
events.detail: The trade-off table: sliding window = lowest fidelity, simplest; summary = balanced; external store = highest fidelity, retrieved on demand, heaviest to build.

events.label: The privacy boundary
events.detail: Cross-session memory and user profiles: the longer and broader the storage, the heavier the privacy duty — retention periods, purpose, and user deletion rights must be explicit engineering.
